h1: Personal Services Business Risk for Incorporated Contractors in Ontario
faq_pairs: Is every incorporated contractor a personal services business?

No. A corporation carries on a PSB only if the person doing the work, or a related person, owns 10% or more of any class of its shares, and the person doing the work would reasonably be regarded as the client's employee if the corporation did not exist. Many contractors have facts on both sides, which is why each relationship needs review.
How much more tax does a PSB pay in Ontario?

The combined rate on PSB income is 44.5%, compared with the current small business rate of 11.2%. On $150,000 of income kept in the corporation, that is $66,750 instead of $16,800, a difference of $49,950 in one year.
Can a PSB still deduct its expenses?

Only a few. Section 18(1)(p) allows salary and benefits paid to the incorporated employee, certain costs of selling property or negotiating contracts that an employee could deduct, and legal costs to collect amounts owed for the services. Rent, software, equipment, travel, phone, insurance and accounting fees are denied.
Does a 40 hour contract make my corporation a PSB?
Not by itself. Fixed hours, set schedules and client-approved timesheets point toward control, but hours alone never decide PSB status. CRA looks at the whole relationship, year by year.
Will a CPT1 ruling settle my PSB status?
No. A CPT1 ruling deals with CPP and EI status. It is not a PSB ruling for income tax, although CRA looks at similar facts. We review whether a CPT1 request is useful in your facts.
Can you make sure my corporation is never treated as a PSB?

No one can promise that. We help you reduce the risk by reviewing your contract and working facts as part of tax planning, documenting how you really work, and supporting your position if CRA asks questions.
Do you work with contractors who are not incorporated?
No. For these services we work only with incorporated Canadian businesses. If you have not incorporated yet, we can help with incorporation first.

h1: 40 Hour Contract PSB Risk: What Fixed Hours Mean for Your Corporation
faq_pairs: Does a 40 hour contract make my corporation a personal services business?
Not by itself. A 40 hour week is one control fact. CRA looks at the whole relationship, including control, tools, chance of profit and risk of loss, and integration, and asks whose business it is.
Is a 37.5 hour contract lower risk than a 40 hour contract?
Not on its own. The difference in hours is small. What matters more is whether the hours are a billing cap or a required schedule, and what the rest of the relationship looks like.
Does timesheet approval by the end client add to PSB risk?

It can. If an end client manager approves your time and supervises your work like staff, it points to control. If the timesheet is only used by the agency for billing, it carries less weight. We note who approves and why.
I must use the client's laptop and VPN. Is that a problem?

It is a control indicator, because the client decides your tools and access. Banks, insurers and governments often require this from every outside firm for security reasons. We document the reason and the tools your corporation does pay for.
If CRA finds my corporation is a PSB, what rate applies?

PSB income is taxed at a combined 44.5% in Ontario. The current small business rate, from July 1, 2026, is 11.2%. On $150,000 kept in the corporation, that means $66,750 of tax instead of $16,800. Section 18(1)(p) also denies most expenses.
Is PSB status decided once for the whole contract?
No. It is tested year by year, for each taxation year of your corporation. A renewal, a new manager or a move to full-time onsite work can change the facts for that year.
Can you change the hours clause in my contract?

No. We are accountants, not lawyers, so any change to contract wording is for your lawyer. As part of tax planning, we review the hours clause and how you actually work, and tell you which facts to document.
Should I file Form CPT1 to get a ruling?
A CPT1 ruling deals with CPP and EI status, not PSB status for income tax, though CRA looks at similar facts. We review whether it is useful in your facts before you decide.

h1: Staffing Agency Contractor Tax for Incorporated Contractors in Ontario
faq_pairs: Do I need to be incorporated to contract through a staffing agency?

Not always. Many agencies offer a T4 payroll option as well as a contract with your corporation. If you choose the corporate route, the agency will ask for proof of incorporation, your business number and your HST number. Our services are for incorporated businesses, and we can also set up the corporation for you.
Does working through an agency protect my corporation from PSB status?

No. On paper the agency receives your services, but CRA looks at the party the services are really provided to, which is usually the end client. The agency contract and the end client's onboarding rules both matter. CRA tests the whole relationship, year by year.
Does my corporation have to charge HST to the agency?

Once your corporation is registered, yes. The rate in Ontario is 13%. A corporation must register once its taxable supplies go over $30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters. A full-time agency contract passes that quickly, and most agencies ask for your HST number before the first invoice.
Will the agency deduct tax from payments to my corporation?

No. The agency pays your corporation its fees plus HST, with no income tax, CPP or EI taken off. Your corporation is responsible for its own corporate tax, its HST returns and the payroll for any salary it pays you.
What happens to my business expenses if CRA finds a PSB?

Section 18(1)(p) limits deductions to salary, wages and other pay to the incorporated employee, benefits and allowances provided to that person, certain costs of selling property or negotiating contracts that an employee could deduct, and legal costs to collect fees owed. Rent, software, equipment, travel, phone, insurance, accounting fees and similar costs are denied.
Can you review my agency contract for PSB indicators?

We review your contract and working facts as part of tax planning, including how the agency contract and the end client's onboarding rules read for control, tools and integration. We are accountants, not lawyers. Contract wording changes are for your lawyer.

If the corporation is not a PSB, the combined Ontario small business rate is 11.2% from July 1, 2026. Income earned before that date was taxed at 12.2%, so a December 31, 2026 year-end gets a blended 11.70%. If the corporation is a PSB, the combined rate is 44.5%.

h1: PSB Tax Cost Calculator for Ontario Contractor Corporations
faq_pairs: What rates does the PSB tax cost calculator use?

For a corporation that is not a PSB, it uses 9% federal plus the Ontario small business rate (3.2% before July 1, 2026 and 2.2% from July 1, 2026) on the first $500,000, and 26.5% above that. For a PSB, it uses 44.5% on all taxable income.
Why does a December 31, 2026 year-end show 11.70%?
That taxation year has 181 days before July 1, 2026 at 12.2% and 184 days from July 1, 2026 at 11.2%. The day-weighted rate is 11.69589%, which the calculator shows as 11.70%.
Why does the PSB column ignore my business expenses?

Paragraph 18(1)(p) of the Income Tax Act denies most PSB expenses, such as rent, software, equipment, phone, insurance and accounting fees. Salary, wages, benefits and allowances paid to the incorporated employee stay deductible, along with a few narrow items.
Does paying myself a salary remove PSB risk?

No. Salary is deductible even for a PSB, so it reduces the corporate income taxed at 44.5%. It does not change whether your corporation is a PSB, and the salary is taxed personally at your marginal rate.
Does the calculator include personal tax, CPP or EI?
No. It shows corporate tax only. It leaves out personal tax on salary or dividends, CPP, EI and the passive income rules. Please book a consultation if you want the full picture for your facts.
Can I use the calculator if my corporation is not in Ontario?
It uses Ontario rates only. Other provinces have different small business and general rates, so the results would not match a corporation taxed in another province.
Does the calculator save the numbers I enter?
No. The calculator runs in your browser. It does not store your inputs or send them to us.

h1: Salary vs Dividend for Incorporated Contractors in Ontario
faq_pairs: Is salary deductible if my corporation is a personal services business?

Yes. Section 18(1)(p) still allows salary, wages or other remuneration paid in the year to the incorporated employee, plus the cost of benefits or allowances provided to that person. Most other costs, such as rent, software, equipment, travel and phone, are denied. That is why salary matters so much in a PSB.
Are dividends from my contractor corporation eligible or non-eligible?

If the corporation is not a PSB and its income is taxed at 11.2% with the small business deduction, dividends from that income are generally non-eligible. If the corporation is a PSB, its income is taxed at the full rate and adds to GRIP, so dividends paid from it can be designated eligible.
Does paying myself a salary reduce my PSB risk?

No. Salary does not change whether your corporation is a PSB. That depends on the whole working relationship, tested year by year. What salary does is reduce the income left in the corporation that would be taxed at 44.5% if CRA reassessed it as a PSB.
How much RRSP room does salary from my corporation create?

New RRSP room is 18% of the prior year's earned income, up to the annual dollar limit, less any pension adjustment. A $120,000 salary creates $21,600 of room for the next year. Dividends are not earned income, so they create no room.
Do I have to pay CPP on salary from my own corporation?

Yes. Salary is pensionable, so the corporation withholds the employee share of CPP, pays the employer share and remits both to CRA. Dividends are not subject to CPP. We include CPP when we compare salary and dividends for you.
What changes for non-eligible dividends on January 1, 2027?

Ontario cuts its non-eligible dividend tax credit from 2.9863% to 1.9863%. The top Ontario marginal rate on non-eligible dividends rises from 47.74% in 2026 to 48.89%. If you were planning a dividend near year-end, we review whether paying it in December 2026 or January 2027 suits you better.
Can you run payroll for my contractor corporation?

Yes. We set up salary, remit source deductions and file T4 slips for incorporated businesses. We work with corporations only, not individuals or sole proprietors, on a fixed flat fee. Please book a consultation and we will look at your pay mix with you.

h1: CRA PSB Review: What to Expect, Stage by Stage
faq_pairs: How does a CRA PSB review usually start?

Usually with a letter, or a call followed by a letter, naming your corporation and the years under review. It often includes a questionnaire about your working relationship: hours, supervision, tools, other clients and who bears the risk.
What documents does CRA usually ask for in a PSB review?

The agency agreement, statements of work, invoices, timesheets, onboarding emails from the end client, details of your equipment and a list of other clients. The auditor may also ask for the general ledger and bank statements.
How long do I have to respond to a CRA proposal letter?
The proposal letter states its own deadline, so please read it the day it arrives. If you need more time, we can ask the auditor before the deadline passes. CRA decides whether to allow it.
What is the deadline after a notice of reassessment?

A notice of objection is generally due within 90 days of the date on the notice of reassessment. Arrears interest applies to the balance owing. Please do not wait until the end of that period to look at your options.
How many years can CRA review?

For a Canadian-controlled private corporation, CRA can generally reassess a year within three years of the date of the original notice of assessment. Some situations extend that period. Each year is tested on its own facts.
Is a CRA PSB review the same as a CPP/EI ruling?

No. Form CPT1 is used to request a CPP/EI ruling on a worker's status. That ruling deals with CPP and EI, not PSB status for income tax, though CRA looks at similar facts. We review whether it is useful in your facts.
Can you promise CRA will accept our position?
No. Nobody can promise an outcome. We make sure CRA sees the real facts, organized and supported by documents, and we respond to each request and to the proposal letter on time.
Do you represent individuals in a CRA PSB review?

No. We work with incorporated Canadian businesses only, and we do not take individuals or sole proprietors as clients for these services. In a PSB review, we act as the corporation's representative with CRA.

h1: What Is a Personal Services Business in Canada? A CPA Explains for IT Contractors
faq_pairs: Is a personal services business the same as being an employee?

No. A PSB is a classification of your corporation's business for income tax. Your corporation still earns the income and files a T2 return. It loses the small business deduction, pays a combined 44.5% in Ontario, and can deduct only the limited items allowed by section 18(1)(p).
Does owning less than 10% of the shares take me out of the definition?

Only if neither you nor anyone related to you is a specified shareholder. Shares can be held directly or indirectly, and shares held by a spouse or another related person can count. In a one-person IT corporation, this part of the definition is almost always met.
Can an IT contractor with more than one client still carry on a PSB?
Yes. Other clients help show that you run your own business, but they do not settle the question. CRA looks at how each engagement actually works, year by year.
What tax rate applies to PSB income in Ontario?
A combined 44.5%, made up of 33% federal tax and Ontario's 11.5% general rate. The current small business rate it replaces is 11.2%, which applies from July 1, 2026.
Does the more-than-five-employees exception help a typical IT contractor?

Rarely. It needs more than five full-time employees in the business throughout the year, which means at least six. Whether owners or family members count depends on their real roles, so it needs review.
Can a CPT1 ruling tell me whether my corporation is a PSB?
No. A CPT1 ruling deals with CPP and EI status for a worker. It is not a PSB ruling for income tax, although CRA looks at similar facts. We review whether a CPT1 request is useful in your facts.

Not by itself. Fixed hours are a control fact. CRA weighs control together with tools, chance of profit and risk of loss, and integration, and asks whose business it is.
If my spouse owns the shares, can I still be an incorporated employee?
Yes. The ownership link is met when you or a person related to you, such as your spouse, owns 10% or more of any class of shares, directly or indirectly.
When I work through an agency, who is the client for the test?

Is a 35 hour contract safer than a 40 hour contract?

Not in itself. Both read as standard full-time schedules. A 35 hour week produces less revenue, so less income is exposed if CRA finds a PSB. At $95 an hour over 48 weeks, the extra tax is $54,154.80 at 35 hours and $61,747.20 at 40 hours in my example.
Does timesheet approval by the end client decide the control question?

No. Any business billing by the hour needs the client to confirm hours before it is paid. What matters is what the approval is used for. Confirming billable hours reads as billing. Reviewing your attendance, tasks and performance reads as supervision.
How does CRA view core hours and on-call rotations?

Core hours and on-call duties are control facts when the client sets them the same way it does for its own staff. They read more like a business service when they are written into your corporation's contract, priced by your corporation and limited to what the project needs.
What tax rate applies if CRA decides my corporation is a PSB?

The combined Ontario PSB rate is 44.5%: 33% federal, including the additional 5% under section 123.5, plus the 11.5% Ontario general rate. If the corporation is not a PSB, the current combined small business rate is 11.2%. Section 18(1)(p) also denies most expenses for a PSB.
Can you change my contract hours clause for me?

No. We are accountants, not lawyers, and contract wording is for your lawyer. We review your contract and working facts as part of tax planning, explain how the hours terms read for tax, and help you keep records that support your position.

meta_description: The PSB tax rate in Ontario is 44.5% vs 11.2% for small business income from July 1, 2026. See how 44.5% is built, the 11.70% blend and worked examples.
featured_image_headline: Line 1: PSB Tax Rate in Ontario for 2026 / Line 2: 44.5% vs 11.2%, With Numbers
author_line: Written by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Canada and USA). Reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA, Founder and Managing Director, Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation, CPA Ontario Firm ID 61330051. Last updated: October 16, 2026.
h1: PSB Tax Rate in Ontario for 2026: 44.5% vs 11.2% Explained With Numbers
faq_pairs: What is the PSB tax rate in Ontario for 2026?

The combined federal and Ontario PSB rate is 44.5%. That is 33% federal (38% less the 10% abatement, with no 13% general rate reduction, plus the 5% additional tax under section 123.5) and 11.5% Ontario.
Did the July 1, 2026 Ontario rate cut lower the PSB rate?
No. The cut lowered the Ontario small business rate to 2.2%, down from 3.2%, so the combined small business rate is now 11.2%. A PSB cannot use the small business rate, so its rate stays at 44.5%.
Why is my December 31, 2026 year-end rate 11.70% and not 11.2%?
The cut is prorated by days. Your taxation year has 181 days before July 1, 2026 at 12.2% and 184 days from July 1, 2026 at 11.2%. The day-weighted rate is 11.69589%, shown as 11.70%.
Can a PSB pay eligible dividends?

Yes. PSB income is not eligible for the small business deduction, so it is taxed at the full rate and adds to the general rate income pool (GRIP). Dividends paid from GRIP can be designated as eligible dividends.
Does paying myself a salary reduce PSB tax?
Salary paid to you is still deductible for a PSB under 18(1)(p), so it reduces the income taxed at 44.5%. It does not change whether the corporation is a PSB, and the salary is taxed in your hands.
What changes for non-eligible dividends on January 1, 2027?

Ontario cuts its non-eligible dividend tax credit to 1.9863%, down from 2.9863%. The top Ontario rate on non-eligible dividends rises to 48.89%, up from 47.74% in 2026. Eligible dividends are not affected.

seo_title: Wiebe Door Test: The Four Tests CRA Uses for Contractors
meta_description: The Wiebe Door test and Sagaz in plain words: control, tools, profit and loss, and integration, applied step by step to a hypothetical IT contractor.
featured_image_headline: Line 1: The Wiebe Door Test / Line 2: The Four Tests CRA Uses
author_line: Written by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Canada and USA). Reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA, Founder and Managing Director, Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation, CPA Ontario Firm ID 61330051. Last updated: October 16, 2026.
h1: The Four Tests CRA Uses: Wiebe Door and Sagaz Applied to a Contractor
faq_pairs: What is the Wiebe Door test?

It is a set of factors used to decide whether a worker is an employee or is in business on their own account. The four main factors are control, ownership of tools, chance of profit and risk of loss, and integration. They are weighed together, not one at a time.
How does Sagaz relate to the Wiebe Door test?

Sagaz states the central question: is the person performing the services as a person in business on their own account? It also makes clear that no single factor decides the answer, and it adds hiring helpers, investment and management to the factors CRA weighs.
Which of the four tests matters most?
None of them decides the answer alone. Control is always relevant, but the weight of each factor depends on the facts of the relationship. CRA looks at the whole picture, year by year.
Does a client-supplied laptop make me an employee?

Not by itself. It is a tools indicator. We look at whether the client's device rule is a security policy that applies to every vendor, and at which tools your corporation actually pays for and uses in the work.
Will switching to a fixed-price contract reduce PSB risk?

It can help only if the price, the scope and the risk are real. If the client still approves weekly timesheets and pays for every extra hour, a fixed-price label says very little. It is one fact among many, and it does not decide PSB status alone.
Is a CPT1 ruling the same as a PSB ruling?

No. Form CPT1 is used to request a CPP/EI ruling on a worker's status. That ruling deals with CPP and EI, not with PSB status for income tax, though CRA looks at similar facts. We review whether it is useful in your facts.

seo_title: PSB Employee Exception: Who Qualifies and Who Does Not
meta_description: The PSB employee exception needs more than five full-time employees all year. See who counts, who does not, and why it rarely helps a solo contractor.
featured_image_headline: Line 1: The PSB Employee Exception / Line 2: Who Qualifies and Who Does Not
author_line: Written by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Canada and USA). Reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA, Founder and Managing Director, Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation, CPA Ontario Firm ID 61330051. Last updated: October 20, 2026.
h1: The More-Than-5-Employees PSB Exception: Who Qualifies and Who Does Not
faq_pairs: What is the PSB employee exception?

It is one of two exceptions in the personal services business definition in section 125(7) of the Income Tax Act. A business is not a PSB if the corporation employs in the business, throughout the year, more than five full-time employees. That means at least six full-time employees for the whole year.
Do part-time employees or subcontractors count toward the six?

No. The exception requires full-time employees of your corporation. Part-time staff do not meet the full-time requirement. Subcontractors, freelancers and other incorporated contractors are not your employees, so they do not count either.
Do I count as one of the six employees if I own the corporation?

It depends on your real role. The question is whether you are genuinely a full-time employee working in the business alongside the others. It needs review of your actual duties and hours. For a solo contractor it rarely matters, because you would still need five more full-time employees.
Can I put family members on payroll to meet the exception?

Only real, full-time roles can support the count. We look at what each family member actually does, their hours, whether the pay is reasonable for the work, and the records behind it. Family on payroll without a real full-time role does not meet the test and creates other tax problems.
Is it worth hiring six employees to get out of the PSB rules?

For a solo contractor, almost never. Six full-time salaries of $50,000 cost $300,000 a year, against $49,950 of extra PSB tax on $150,000 of retained income. Hiring only makes sense if those employees do real work that brings in more revenue than they cost.
What is the associated corporation exception?

A business is not a PSB if the amount paid for the services is received from a corporation associated with it in the year. Association is a technical common control test in section 256. It does not help a contractor billing a staffing agency or an unrelated bank, insurer or government client.

seo_title: 12 Contract Clauses That Raise PSB Risk for Contractors
meta_description: 12 contract clauses that raise PSB risk for Ontario IT and finance contractors, why each one matters, what can weigh the other way, and what PSB costs.
featured_image_headline: Line 1: 12 Contract Clauses / Line 2: That Raise PSB Risk
author_line: Written by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Canada and USA). Reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA, Founder and Managing Director, Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation, CPA Ontario Firm ID 61330051. Last updated: October 20, 2026.
h1: 12 Contract Clauses That Raise PSB Risk for IT and Finance Contractors
faq_pairs: Does one of these clauses make my corporation a PSB?

No. Each clause can point toward employment, but CRA weighs control, tools, chance of profit and risk of loss, and integration across the whole relationship, year by year. Many IT and finance contracts contain several of these clauses, so the working facts matter.
Which of the 12 clauses matters most?

There is no fixed ranking. Clauses that require you to do the work personally, or that let the client direct how you work, often go to the heart of the question. Even then, CRA weighs them with everything else.
Can I lower PSB risk by removing these clauses from my contract?

Contract wording is for your lawyer and the agency to agree. We are accountants, not lawyers. Also, CRA tests what actually happens. If the wording changes but the work stays the same, the change carries little weight.
My agency agreement looks fine, but the end client's onboarding papers do not. Which one counts?

Both. With an agency in the middle, CRA asks whether you would reasonably be an employee of the party that really receives your services. The end client's rules on hours, equipment, training and conduct can matter as much as the agency agreement.
Does a client laptop on its own mean my corporation is a PSB?
No. A client laptop with VPN-only access points to the client's tools, and banks and insurers often require it of every vendor. It is one factor, weighed with all the others.
If I pay myself a salary, do these clauses still matter?

Yes. Salary paid to you stays deductible under section 18(1)(p), which reduces the income exposed to the 44.5% rate. Whatever profit stays in the corporation would still be taxed at 44.5% instead of 11.2% if CRA treated it as PSB income.
Can CRA give me a ruling on my contract?

Not a PSB ruling for income tax. Form CPT1 asks CRA for a CPP and EI ruling on a worker's status. That ruling does not decide PSB status, although CRA looks at similar facts. If you are thinking about one, we first review whether it is useful in your facts.

seo_title: Finance Contractor PSB Risk at Banks Through Agencies
meta_description: Finance contractor PSB risk: why the agency does not shield you, how CRA reads bank controls, and what 44.5% vs 11.2% costs on a $163,200 contract.
featured_image_headline: Line 1: Finance Contractors at Banks / Line 2: The PSB Risk Most People Miss
author_line: Written by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Canada and USA). Reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA, Founder and Managing Director, Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation, CPA Ontario Firm ID 61330051. Last updated: October 20, 2026.
h1: Finance Contractors at Banks Through Agencies: The PSB Risk Most People Miss
faq_pairs: Does working through a staffing agency protect my corporation from the PSB rules?

Not on its own. In a three-party arrangement, CRA looks at whether you would reasonably be an employee of the party your services are really provided to. For a finance contractor at a bank, that is usually the bank. The agency contract and the bank's onboarding rules both matter.
Why are finance roles at banks seen as higher PSB risk?

Finance, risk, audit and compliance are core functions of a bank. When your work is part of how the bank closes its books or meets its reporting duties, the integration factor can point toward the bank's business. Bank-run controls and supervision add to the control side.
Does sign-off authority at the bank matter?

It can matter a great deal. Approving journal entries, reconciliations or control tests, or reviewing the bank's own staff, puts you inside the bank's control structure. We note what you approve, under whose authority, and whether it ties to a defined deliverable.
How much more tax would my corporation pay as a PSB?

On $163,200 of billings with $9,000 of expenses, corporate tax is $17,270.40 at 11.2% if it is not a PSB. As a PSB, the expenses are denied and tax at 44.5% is $72,624. That is $55,353.60 more for one year.
Can my corporation deduct its expenses if it is a PSB?

Only a few. Section 18(1)(p) allows salary and other pay to you, the cost of your benefits or allowances, certain costs of selling property or negotiating contracts that an employee could deduct, and legal costs to collect amounts owed. Rent, software, equipment, travel, phone, insurance and accounting fees are denied.
Can you make sure my corporation is not treated as a PSB?
No one can promise that. PSB status depends on the facts, tested year by year. We review your contract and working facts as part of tax planning, tell you what to document and help you reduce risk.
Would a CPT1 ruling settle my PSB status at the bank?
No. A CPT1 ruling deals with CPP and EI status, not PSB status for income tax, though CRA looks at similar facts. If you are considering one, we first review whether it is useful in your facts.

seo_title: PSB Reassessment in Ontario: Denied Deductions, Double Tax
meta_description: In a PSB reassessment, CRA denies the small business deduction and most expenses, and taxes the income at 44.5% in Ontario. See the numbers, line by line.
featured_image_headline: Line 1: PSB Reassessment / Line 2: Denied Deductions and Double Tax
author_line: Written by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Canada and USA). Reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA, Founder and Managing Director, Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation, CPA Ontario Firm ID 61330051. Last updated: October 20, 2026.
h1: What Happens in a PSB Reassessment: Denied Deductions and Double Tax
faq_pairs: What is a PSB reassessment?

It is a notice of reassessment in which CRA re-taxes a corporation's past income as personal services business income. The small business deduction is denied, the Ontario rate becomes 44.5%, and most expenses are denied under section 18(1)(p).
Which expenses are still deductible after a PSB reassessment?

Salary, wages or other remuneration paid in the year to the incorporated employee, the cost of benefits or allowances provided to them, certain amounts spent selling property or negotiating contracts that an employee could deduct, and legal expenses to collect amounts owing for services. Other costs are denied.
How far back can CRA reassess a corporation for PSB?

For a Canadian-controlled private corporation, the normal reassessment period is three years from the date of the original notice of assessment for the year. Some situations allow CRA to go further back, so please check the dates on your own notices.
Does arrears interest apply to a PSB reassessment?
Yes. Arrears interest applies to the extra tax from the date it was originally due until it is paid, and it compounds daily. The oldest year in a reassessment usually carries the most interest.
Why is PSB income said to be taxed twice?

The corporation pays 44.5% on the income, and you pay personal tax again on the dividend. On $100,000 at the top 2026 Ontario rates, the total is $66,333.70, compared with $53,530 if the same amount were paid as salary.
Can dividends paid from PSB income be eligible dividends?

Yes. PSB income is taxed at the full rate, so it adds to the general rate income pool (GRIP), and dividends paid from it can be designated eligible dividends. That narrows the gap with salary but does not close it.
What happens after I receive a notice of reassessment?

The notice shows the revised tax, the balance owing and arrears interest. A notice of objection is generally due within 90 days of the date on the notice of reassessment. Please do not wait until the end of that period to get advice.

h1: PSB Risk Reduction Checklist for Incorporated Contractors
faq_pairs: How often should I go through a PSB risk checklist?
Once a year, ideally before your corporation's year-end, and again whenever you sign a new contract, renew with a new statement of work, or change end clients. PSB status is tested year by year.
If I complete the checklist, is my corporation safe from PSB status?
No. The checklist helps reduce risk and document your position. CRA looks at the whole working relationship each year, and no single document or clause decides the outcome.
What records matter most if CRA asks about PSB?

Your contract and statements of work, numbered invoices, corporate bank statements, equipment and software receipts, evidence of other clients and marketing, payroll records and every CRA letter with your replies.
Does paying myself a salary reduce PSB risk?

Salary does not change whether the corporation is a PSB. It does stay deductible under section 18(1)(p), so it reduces the income taxed at 44.5%. Salary is taxed in your hands, so the mix needs planning.
Can I lower PSB risk by changing my contract wording?
Wording helps only when it matches how the work is really done. CRA looks at the actual relationship. We are accountants, not lawyers, so any change to contract wording is for your lawyer.
Should I ask CRA for a CPT1 ruling?
A CPT1 asks CRA to rule on CPP and EI status. It is not a PSB ruling for income tax, though CRA looks at similar facts. We review whether it is useful in your facts before you decide.
